title: Injective logarithmic charts preserve log regularity and recover divisorial structure
statement: Let $(Y,M_Y)$ and $(X,M_X)$ be locally Noetherian fine saturated log schemes, and let $f:(X,M_X)\to(Y,M_Y)$ be a morphism of log schemes [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. Suppose $(Y,M_Y)$ is log regular in the stratum and dimension sense of that definition. Assume that etale locally on $X,Y$ the morphism has charts $P\to M_Y$, $Q\to M_X$ by fine saturated monoids $P,Q$ (as in that definition) and a homomorphism $g:P\to Q$ compatible with the structure maps and with $f$, for which $g^{\rm gp}:P^{\rm gp}\to Q^{\rm gp}$ is injective and its cokernel is torsion-free, and the comparison morphism $X\to Y\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[P]}\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[Q]$ is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] or etale [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Here $\mathbf Z[S]$ is the monoid ring, freely generated as an abelian group by $[s]$ with $[s][t]=[s+t]$. Then $(X,M_X)$ is log regular. Its triviality locus $U$ is dense open and, for $j:U\hookrightarrow X$, the structure map canonically identifies $M_X$ with $\mathcal O_X\cap j_*\mathcal O_U^\times$. In particular $(X,X\setminus U)$ is a log regular pair [def-trf-log-regular-pair].

source.place: Expose VI 1.8 (log-smooth preservation, printed p. 70), 1.4 (dense triviality locus and recovery of the divisorial structure, printed p. 69), and the injective-chart log-smooth test used in Proposition 1.9, printed p. 71; general chart criterion: Kato, Logarithmic structures of Fontaine--Illusie (1988), Theorem 3.5 (not locally available).
